interest: Shows the Navy's pre-war Japanese-language program training future intelligence officers Biard and Slonim, amid Japan's 1934 status ban.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.32711) documents the assignment of United States Navy officers to Tokyo for Japanese language instruction, as well as earlier diplomatic monitoring of Japanese naval activities. The core of the file, dating from July and August 1939, comprises official correspondence between Acting Secretary of the Navy Charles Edison, Assistant Secretary of State Francis B. Sayre, and American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Tokyo Eugene H. Dooman concerning orders for Lieutenant (jg) Forrest R. Biard and Lieutenant (jg) Gilven M. Slonim to study Japanese in Tokyo under the administrative supervision of the Naval Attaché. The dispatches explicitly address the diplomatic and legal status of these officers, referencing Japan's late-1934 termination of diplomatic privileges for foreign service attachés' language students. Also filed within the bundle is an August 1933 Far Eastern Affairs memorandum summarizing a consular report from Taihoku on a Japanese fleet visit to Taiwan, noting bellicose statements by Japanese admirals regarding strained Japanese-American relations.
